title: Sequence-based degradation plan for Dedicated control planes
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Background: Dedicated control planes host multiple customer tenants with strong performance SLAs. During upgrades, regional network issues, or a noisy neighbor, we need a predictable, incrementally-degrading behavior that preserves critical SLOs for high-tier tenants and allows safe operator action without triggering broad outages. Current approaches (global hard caps or full-tenant quarantine) are too blunt: they either over-protect and reduce capacity or under-protect and allow cascading failures.

Goal: Implement a sequence-based degradation strategy for Dedicated control planes that: preserves P99 latency and availability SLOs for P0/P1 tenants where possible; provides staged degradations (soft throttles, KV cache eviction, lossless request rerouting, then hard shedding as last resort); integrates with rolling upgrade choreography so upgrades can pause or slow per-shard when degradation thresholds are hit; and surfaces deterministic telemetry and runbook triggers for SRE/SEs.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change global billing, user-visible quotas in Console, or per-tenant admission logic for Hosted API. It focuses on Dedicated and Private control-plane runtime behaviors and orchestration hooks.

Design overview:
- Degradation phases (sequence):
  1) Phase A - Preferential batching and KV hinting: increase batching window for best-effort tenants and proactively warm caches for high-tier tenants.
  2) Phase B - Soft per-tenant token limits (grace window): apply token/simultaneous-request soft caps and queue with TTL; longer tail requests are deprioritized.
  3) Phase C - Region-affinity reroute: shift best-effort tenants to adjacent region replicas with lower priority and advertise temporary region-affinity leases to avoid oscillation.
  4) Phase D - Circuit-breaker eviction: tripped tenants are isolated to a degraded lane (no autoscaling), non-critical features (batch-only) disabled.
  5) Phase E - Hard shed/quarantine: final stage only if phase D fails to restore SLOs for critical tenants; this uses strict shunt rules and operator approval.

- SLO-driven transition logic: transitions are driven by an SLO budget funnel computed every 30s from cross-region p95/p99 latency and success rate, weighted by tenant tier. When the funnel falls below configured thresholds, we progress to the next phase. We can automatically step down if metrics recover for a configurable cool-down window.

- Upgrade integration: the rolling-upgrade controller will consult the degradation controller before advancing waves. If a shard is in Phase C or higher, the upgrade wave will pause and either (a) reduce concurrency for the upgrade, or (b) skip/rollback the wave depending on operator policy. This reduces upgrade-induced cascading.

- Observability & tooling:
  - New metrics: degradation_phase{shard,region,tenant_tier}, slo_budget_funnel, phase_transition_events, reroute_decisions (with reason).
  - Dashboards: per-shard phase timelines, per-tenant transition history, upgrade-wave correlation.
  - Alerts: automated runbook link when a shard enters Phase D. Alerts include suggested actions (drain-notify, scale-reserve, roll-back-wave).

Acceptance criteria:
- Control plane can move a shard cleanly through Phase A->E in a simulated noisy-neighbor test without violating P0 tenant P99 > target for more than 2 minutes.
- Rolling upgrades pause automatically when a shard is in Phase C+ and resume when shard recovers.
- Metrics and dashboards ingest new degradation telemetry and show phase timelines for test clusters.
- End-to-end integration test that injects synthetic latency shows orderly tenant-level degradations and provides evidence in CI logs.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Prototype SLO funnel calculation service (stateless, 30s window) and API to query current funnel score per shard.
2) Implement phase controller modules with idempotent commands to change shard state and persist current phase in control plane state store.
3) Wire upgrade controller to consult phase API and support pause/retry policies.
4) Add per-tenant soft quotas and prioritized batching hooks in runtime admission layer.
5) Implement region-affinity reroute policies and low-priority lanes.
6) Add metrics, dashboards, and runbook links.
7) End-to-end staging run with chaos (latency, packet loss, noisy tenant) and refine thresholds.

Rollout plan:
- Milestone 1 (canary): deploy funnel service + read-only phase telemetry in staging clusters, verify dashboards. (1 week)
- Milestone 2 (soft enforcement): enable Phase A/B for best-effort tenants in a single dedicated cluster, closely monitor. (2 weeks)
- Milestone 3 (upgrade integration): safe pause during upgrade waves in two additional clusters. (2 weeks)
- Milestone 4 (full enforcement): enable full sequence in all Dedicated clusters with operator controls and gradual tenant expansion. (4 weeks)

Testing strategy: unit tests for funnel logic; integration tests simulating multiple tenants and latency patterns; staging chaos experiment (Gremlin/chaos-mesh) to validate transitions; post-deploy monitoring for 72 hours.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: oscillation between regions during reroute. Mitigation: region-affinity leases with exponential backoff and a jittered cool-down.
- Risk: incorrect weighting causing lower-tier tenants to starve critical resources. Mitigation: conservative default weights and disable automatic hard-shed for first release.
- Risk: complex operator UX for pause/resume. Mitigation: Build simple runbook buttons (Pause/Force-Rollback) in Console and expose clear incident playbook.

Related docs: Confluence: /spaces/RELIABILITY/pages/Sequence+Degradation+Plan, Prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4213 (WIP).
